The '''2015 Transnistrian census''' was organized in the unrecognized state of [[Transnistria]] in 2015. It was held after [[Moldova]], internationally recognized as the owner of the state's territory, made [[2014 Moldovan census|a census]] in 2014.

==Census results==
According to the census results, [[Transnistria]]'s population was of 475,373 people in 2015. This represented a population decline of 14.47%<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://privetpmr.ru/perepis-naseleniya-pmr|title=Перепись населения ПМР|website=Privet PMR|date=9 March 2017|language=ru|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180814231257/http://privetpmr.ru/perepis-naseleniya-pmr|archive-date=14 August 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> (or nearly 80,000 people) since the [[2004 Transnistrian census]], which is an amount similar to the population of the second largest Transnistrian-controlled city, [[Bender, Moldova|Bender]] (Tighina).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://moldova.europalibera.org/a/27759054.html|title=Transnistria a pierdut "un oraș"|first=Radu|last=Benea|publisher=[[Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty|Radio Europa Liberă Moldova]]|date=16 May 2016|language=ro}}</ref>

The ethnic composition results were the following:<ref name=":0" />
* [[Russians]]: 29.1%
* [[Moldovans]]: 28.6%
* [[Ukrainians]]: 22.9%
* [[Bulgarians]]: 2.4%
* [[Gagauz people|Gagauz]]: 1.1%
* [[Belarusians]]: 0.5%
* Transnistrians: 0.2%
* Others: 1.4%

This census was the first one in Transnistria in which the population was given the option to identify as "Transnistrian", which more than 1,000 people did. Furthermore, 14% of the population did not specify its ethnic affiliation.<ref name=":0" />
